class.name: NetwSession
class.brief_description: The players, scenes and signals of a [member Node.multiplayer] session.
class.description:
Reached with [method Netw.session] from any [Node]. Mostly useful for connecting signals. [codeblock] var s := Netw.session(self) s.entered.connect(on_entered) s.exited.connect(on_exited) for player: NetwPlayer in s.players: scoreboard.add(player)
func on_exited(reason: NetwSession.ExitReason, detail: String) -> void: if reason == NetwSession.KICKED: show_message("Kicked: %s" % detail) [/codeblock] There is one handle per session, so it is safe to keep it across an await. Connecting is done as you would normally do with [SceneMultiplayer], by assigning [member MultiplayerAPI.multiplayer_peer]. [member connection] finds servers and joins or hosts one, and [method Netw.prepare_join] names the player who joins. [b]Moving the server[/b] The session survives the server leaving when its [MultiplayerPeer] can hand the server role to another peer. Such a peer declares this signal, and [method transfer_server] works when it also has the method. [codeblock] signal server_relabelled(successor_was: int, former_now: int)
func transfer_server(peer_id: int) -> Error: pass [/codeblock] The peer emits the signal from its own [method MultiplayerPeer.poll], once it already answers the new ids. [NakamaWrapper] does this when [member NakamaWrapper.migrate_on_host_loss] is on. ENet, WebRTC, Steam and [OfflineMultiplayerPeer] do not, so losing the server ends the session.

method.name: bucket_of
method.description: The per-peer game data of [param type] stored for [param peer], created on first use. See [method NetwMultiplayer.peer_get_bucket].

method.name: create_scene
method.description: Spawns [param scene] as a new scene with no players in it. [param isolation] decides whether it has its own physics and rendering world. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: database
method.description: The database declared as [param name] with [method Netw.configure_database], or [code]null[/code] when there is none.

method.name: find_scene
method.description: Returns the newest scene whose root node is named [param label], or [code]null[/code].

method.name: install_physics_stepper
method.description: Lets [param stepper] step the physics of [param world] in place of [code]PhysicsServer3D.space_step[/code], for a physics server without it. Pass [code]null[/code] as [param stepper] to remove it. [codeblock] func _ready() -> void: session.install_physics_stepper(get_world_3d(), MyStepper.new()) [/codeblock]

method.name: interest_layer
method.description: The [NetwInterestLayer] called [param name], created on first use.

method.name: kick
method.description: Removes [param player] from the session and disconnects their peer with [param reason]. The server's own player cannot be kicked, use [method leave] instead. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: leave
method.description: Leaves the session. The server saves its entity rows first, and stays online if the database refuses a row. The promise resolves with an [enum @GlobalScope.Error] once the peer is down or the save failed.

method.name: player_of
method.description: The [NetwPlayer] of [param peer], [code]null[/code] when there is none.

method.name: register_service
method.description: Registers [param service] so [method service] returns it. [param type] defaults to the script of [param service]. A [NetwService] registers itself.

method.name: save_entities
method.description: Saves every entity row that changed since its last save, including rows of entities that already left. Call it again to retry a row the database refused. [method leave] runs the same save. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK every changed row is stored ┠╴ERR_UNAUTHORIZED this peer is not the server ┠╴ERR_UNCONFIGURED this handle outlived its session ┖╴a row's code the first row still unsaved, see NetwPersistence.save [/codeblock] [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: service
set_peer_bandwidth
method.description: Gives [param peer] its own budget in kbit/s, in place of [member NetwSessionConfig.bandwidth_kbps], for what this peer sends it. [code]0[/code] returns it to the session's budget, and a negative value is refused. The budget lasts until [param peer] disconnects. [codeblock] Netw.session(self).set_peer_bandwidth(player.peer_id, 64) [/codeblock]

method.name: set_server_info
method.description: Replaces what this session advertises about itself, such as the name shown in a server list. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: table
method.description: The table of the schema declared as [param name] with [method Netw.configure_schema], or [code]null[/code] when there is none.

method.name: transfer_server
method.description: Asks the transport to make [param peer_id] the server and this peer a client under a new id. [signal server_transferred] follows on every peer. Whether a transport can is stated in the class description. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴ERR_UNAUTHORIZED called on a client ┠╴ERR_UNAVAILABLE the transport cannot move the server ┠╴ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER peer_id is not a connected client ┖╴ERR_BUSY a database still has writes to settle [/codeblock] [b]Server Only.[/b]

members.member: A copy of the [NetwSessionConfig] this session was configured with. Writing to it changes nothing, use [method Netw.configure_session] before connecting and [method set_server_info] after.
The [NetwConnection] of this session, to find servers and create peers.
[code]true[/code] when this peer has its own player, at [constant ROLE_CLIENT] and [constant ROLE_LISTEN_SERVER].
Whether a peer is assigned and connected. It stays [code]true[/code] until [signal exited], so it is still [code]true[/code] while [signal exiting] runs and the session's scenes are freed.
The [NetwPlayer] of this peer, [code]null[/code] until [signal local_joined].
Every [NetwPlayer] that has joined, including those whose peer has since disconnected. See [member NetwMultiplayer.connected_players] for only the connected ones.
What this peer is in the session.
The [Node] replicated nodes are under, [code]null[/code] when the session is not in the tree.
Every live scene. Use [method find_scene] to find one by name.
Every counter this session keeps, keyed by [enum NetwMultiplayer.Stat].

signal.name: entered
signal.description: Emitted when this peer is online.

signal.name: exited
signal.description: Emitted after the session is cleaned up, with the same [param reason] and [param detail] as [signal exiting].

signal.name: exiting
signal.description: Emitted before the session is cleaned up, so [member players] and [member scenes] can still be read. [param detail] is the message the server gave, if any.

signal.name: join_failed
signal.description: This peer's join was rejected with [param code] and the [param reason] the server gave. [member local_player] stays [code]null[/code].

signal.name: local_joined
signal.description: The [NetwPlayer] of this peer has joined. [member local_player] is set from here on.

signal.name: player_joined
signal.description: A [NetwPlayer] has joined, including this peer's own.

signal.name: player_left
signal.description: A [NetwPlayer] has left, either because their peer disconnected or because of [method kick]. [member NetwPlayer.is_active] is already [code]false[/code].

signal.name: scene_ready
signal.description: Emitted after the root of [param scene] is ready, so the whole scene can be accessed. [codeblock] func on_scene_ready(arena: NetwScene) -> void: arena.root.get_node(^"Spawns").arrange() [/codeblock]

signal.name: server_transferred

constants.constant: Hosting or joining, and may still fail.
A client. A listen server also has a player, so check [member is_local_client] for that.
A server with no local player.
A server that also has a player.
This peer left with [method leave] or cleared its peer.
The server announced it was shutting down.
The connection dropped with no warning.
The server kicked this peer with [method kick].
Another peer was assigned to [member MultiplayerAPI.multiplayer_peer].

When the server moves, each client frees the entities it received and gets the new server's world again as new nodes, and the entities a client spawned itself are despawned. The [NetwClock] of each peer holds until that peer has the world back. [method Netw.configure_transfer] picks what the new server keeps.
Each client keeps its world and its nodes.
